title: SHCT — Slug–Hydrate Coupled-Transient solver

creators.name: Onyejekwe, Akosa Samuel
creators.affiliation: Cyprus University of Technology, Limassol, Cyprus

description:
A one-dimensional transient solver that carries the slug field and the hydrate field of a subsea multiphase pipeline in a single integration: holdup transport, conservative gas-mass continuity, an implicit pressure equation, energy transport and an advected hydrate phase field, closed by published correlations and a multicomponent Peng–Robinson flash, and advanced over a Monte-Carlo ensemble that returns a probabilistic time-to-plug.

v3.3.0 — the coupling criterion is now derived rather than imposed. This is the substantive change in this release, and it changes what kind of claim the work makes. ΦSH was wired into the deposition in three places: consolidation required ΦSH > 1, the wall-capture fraction was scaled by clip(ΦSH − 1, 0, 1) so nothing deposited below 1 at all, and erosion ran only below 1. Together they made ΦSH = 1 a switch between "no deposit" and "unopposed deposit", so the criterion the study reports was an INPUT: no result the solver could produce would have contradicted it. The central claim was unfalsifiable by construction rather than merely unvalidated.

All three are removed. Deposition and slug scouring now compete continuously and ΦSH drives no term in the solver. Setting dδ/dt = 0 gives a finite equilibrium thickness δeq = ΦSH · δref with δref = fwallD/(4 Cφ kero) = 21.2 mm on this line, so ΦSH is the equilibrium deposit thickness in units of δref — the physical content Cφ carried all along without stating it. Growth runs away once that equilibrium passes the consolidation restriction, at Φcrit = 2 Cφ kero rconsol/fwall = 1.08, derived from three kinetic constants. That it lands within 8 % of unity is now a result rather than a definition, and it is falsifiable: a flow loop can measure whether growth stalls at δeq.

Hydrate mass conservation. Making erosion unconditional exposed a leak that took three attempts to close, each measured rather than assumed. Scoured deposit was being annihilated (10.3 % of all hydrate formed); routing it into the bulk phase field pushed φ past its packing cap and destroyed 35 %; returning the rejected fraction to the wall left 8 % in cells whose wall was also at δmax. A saturated slurry cannot entrain more, so scouring is now capped by the carrying headroom. That closes it completely on any case that does not plug — the mitigated scenario reports 1.9e-25, and the reference regression case 5.7e-26 — but NOT on the as-operated case study, which still loses 8 %, in cells where the wall has reached delta_max and the bulk phi_max simultaneously and there is genuinely nowhere left to put the mass. That residue is reported in every summary as hydrate_packing_clip_frac, it does not affect the engineering answer (the line blocks at a P50 of 3.2 h, long before those cells saturate), and its mechanism has not been attributed. None of this was visible until the measurement went in with the first change.

Verified against something other than itself. Ransom's water-faucet problem — the standard assessment case for RELAP5-3D, MARS and TRACE, with a closed-form solution — is reproduced at an observed L1 convergence order of 1.04, 6.1× more accurately than first-order upwind. The scope is stated rather than glossed: this solver is drift-flux, so it cannot close the faucet's momentum problem; what is tested is the holdup transport, via the production code path. Separately, five findings reported in published flow-loop studies are reproduced (steady-state thickness, subcooling, shear stripping, MEG, azimuthal skew) — directions only, the numeric series being paywalled and not reproduced here, and four of the five weak enough that most plausible deposition models would also reproduce them. The steady-state thickness is the one that discriminates: the gated formulation could not have produced a plateau at all.

Case study. P50 time-to-plug moves 2.8 → 3.2 h, max subcooling 21 → 17.6 °C, MEG dose 60 → 56 wt%. Plug probability (100 %) and peak deposit (117 mm) are unchanged. Every movement was attributed before the regression baseline was rewritten.

What is still not established. Φcrit is derived and falsifiable, which is not the same as confirmed: it has not been measured, and C, n and kg0 are fitted to no dataset. There is no whole-system comparison against a licensed transient multiphase code. One verification check remains INCONCLUSIVE (thermal relaxation, 6.188 % NRMSE, unattributed after grid refinement ruled out discretisation). The liquid-bounds discard is 5.85 % on the production case, reported openly. Hydrate mass is conserved exactly unless the bore plugs, where 8 % is lost in cells the model has already declared solid and the mechanism is not yet attributed. Treat this as a hypothesis with a verified solver behind it, not a calibrated predictor.

This release archives the exact code, input deck and generated outputs behind the manuscript A dimensionless coupling number for the competition between hydrate deposition and slug renewal in subsea multiphase pipelines.
